question: What do our procedures say about remote access, and what does CIP require of it?
answer:
The requirements for remote access are primarily governed by **CIP-005-7**, while our internal procedures for managing these sessions are detailed in the **LSPG Bomgar Remote Access Session Work Instruction** and the **LSPG Electronic Security Perimeter and IRA Procedure**.

### NERC CIP Requirements (CIP-005-7)
The standard focuses on managing **Interactive Remote Access** to BES Cyber Systems. Specifically, **R2 Part 2.4** requires that the entity "Have one or more methods for determining active vendor remote access sessions (including Interactive Remote Access and system-to-system remote access)" [cite R-0dd4f7].

### Our Internal Procedures
Our procedures address both the monitoring of sessions and the controls used during emergency access:

*   **Session Monitoring:** The **LSPG Bomgar Remote Access Session Work Instruction** includes a traceability mapping for **CIP-005-7 R2 Part 2.4**. It specifies that for High Impact BCS and associated PCA, as well as Medium Impact BCS with External Routable Connectivity, the entity uses "Section 3.1" and "3.1.1" and "3.1.2" to address the requirement for determining active sessions [cite O-2dd4f7].
*   **Emergency Access Controls:** The **LSPG Electronic Security Perimeter and IRA Procedure** defines specific controls for "Emergency interactive access to CIP Cyber Assets within an ESP" [cite O-fb3ce0]. These include:
    *   The use of an "LSPG owned computer/laptop" [cite O-fb3ce0].
    *   The use of "Non-routable access to CIP Cyber Asset within an ESP (for example, but not limited to, serial console/RS-232/KVM/maintenance port)" [cite O-fb3ce0].
    *   Strict limitations on **session sharing** for remote user assistance: sharing is only permitted if the remote user has a "need to know" and "has read-only access to the sharing session" [cite O-fb3ce0].

I have not read the specific content of the "Section 3.1" or "3.1.1" mentioned in the Bomgar Work Instruction, so I cannot describe the exact technical method used to determine active sessions beyond what is noted in the traceability table.

Quoted sources:
- "CIP-005 Interactive Remote Access Management – R2. Each Responsible Entity allowing Interactive Remote Access to BES Cyber Systems shall implement one or more documented processes that collectively include the applicable requirement parts, where technically feasible. R2 Part 2.4 Have one or more methods for determining active vendor remote access sessions (including Interactive Remote Access and system-to_system remote access). Section 3.1 High Impact BCS and associated PCA Medium Impact BCS with External Routable Connectivity and associated PCA Yes" (LSPG User Open RDP Session Report Work Instruction v4.pdf — Appendix 1: Requirements Traceability)
- "3.3.4 Control and Authentication 3.3.4.1 Emergency interactive access to CIP Cyber Assets within an ESP shall utilize the following access controls: • Emergency interactive access shall utilize an LSPG owned computer/laptop. • Non-routable access to CIP Cyber Asset within an ESP (for example, but not limited to, serial console/RS- 232/KVM/maintenance port). • Emergency interactive access session sharing is permitted for remote user assistance and/or verification, when all of the following apply to the remote user: o The remote user has a “need to know”. o The remote user has read-only access to the sharing session." (LSPG Electronic Security Perimeter and IRA Procedure v11.pdf — 3.3.4 Control and Authentication)
